observations: L04, L09: long joins (عـن, وبَيَّنَّاهمـا) are not transcribed; nor the long kāf of تستكمل (L05).

The page has ten lines of text in a column at the upper right (337 to 503 pt) and the figure for the moon's light of chapter 30, which stands at the left of the column and fills the page under it; it has no heading, no rule, no notes and no printer's signature. L10 is short (it begins at the right edge and ends at 429 pt) and closes the text with a full stop. The folio number «f. 64,v.» stands in the right margin beside L01, where an asterisk marks the folio's first word وقد (the note on p. 93 says that f. 64,r. holds nothing). Nallino's line numbers 5 and 10 stand at the far left of the page (63 to 72 pt), beyond the figure.

Figure F01 (redrawn; its measures and the way they were taken are in the geometry). At the top the circle of the sun (radius 48.5 pt) with the word «الشمس» across the axis, its level diameter with ا at its left end and ج at its right end, both outside the circle, and ب under the diameter at the left of the centre. The upright axis runs from the top of the sun's circle down to the line ك ط of the lowest circle of the moon; on it, 146 pt above that circle's centre, the earth is a filled disc (radius 3.1 pt) with the word «الارض» at its left and the letter ي at its right below it. Ten circles of the moon (radius 24.6 to 25.1 pt) stand side by side, touching or within 0.7 pt of one another, their centres 20 degrees apart on the left half of a circle of 145.0 pt about the earth. In every circle the line ك ط bounds the dark half, which is hatched with thin upright lines and lies away from the sun; in the eight circles between the first and the last a second line, م ل, crosses the whole circle at right angles to the direction of the earth. A dashed arc joins the first circle to the last at the right of the axis, and along it, turned a quarter and read downward, stand the words «وحكم هذا النصف مثل النصف الآخر» (the madda of الآخر is printed; no other signs).

Figure F01, its letters (59 letters and words; those in the dark halves are printed over the hatching). First circle, at the top (the conjunction): in the lit half ك, then ن at the right of the axis, then ط; in the dark half ل under the ك, the word «مظلم» across the axis and م under the ط. Circles 2 to 6: ك at the upper left end of the line ك ط (inside the second circle, outside the others), ط near its right end, د over the centre, م in the lit half by the line م ل and ل in the dark half. Circles 7 to 9: ك outside at the left, ط and د as before, and the two other letters changed about: ل in the lit half and م in the dark half. Last circle, at the foot (the opposition): in the lit half ك and the word «منير» across the axis, in the dark half ل under the ك and ز at the centre, where the axis ends; ط and م stand outside the circle at the right, the ط above the line ك ط and the م under it. The note on p. 93 says that the letters are wanting in the codex and in Plato's version and were restored by Nallino, and that the lines from ا to ك and from ج to ط are left out.

The numerals in letters, each under its bar: {ov:قف} 180 (L05, bar 13.2 pt): the qāf, with its two dots (2.2 x 1.4 pt), is joined to a final fā' that is printed without its dot, in both copies; the letter of the numeral is kept (100 and 80: fifteen times twelve, as the sentence says). {ov:يب} 12 (L07, bar 13.3 pt): the yā' with its two dots under it joined to the bā' with its dot.
Final yā': with its two dots in الذي, التي (L02, L05) and اثنَيْ (L04); without dots in يُرَى (L02), الى (L05), وعلى (L08) and تعالى (L10).
L01: تَبَيَّنَ: fathas over the tā', the bā' and the nūn and, over the yā', a shadda with a fatha above it (two marks). ظهَر: a fatha over the hā'. انّ: a shadda over the nūn.

L02: دائرة (L02, L06) and الدائرتَيْن (L09): the hamza over its tooth. Over the qāf of القمر, above its two dots, a speck (1.1 x 1.1 pt, 12.6 to 13.7 pt over the baseline) that the second copy does not have; it is not transcribed. يُرَى: a damma over the yā', its tail printed apart from its head, and a short fatha over the rā'.

L03: الضَّوْء: over the ḍād a shadda with a fatha above it (two marks), a round sukun over the wāw and the bare hamza on the line. كاملًا: over the lām-alif the fathatan, printed small (2.9 x 1.8 pt), its two strokes run together, in both copies. خَمْسَةَ: the fatha over the khā' and the round sukun over the mīm are joined in one mark (5.0 x 2.9 pt), a fatha stands over the sīn and a short fatha (1.4 x 1.4 pt) over the two dots of the tā' marbūṭa; خمسة (L07): no signs. عَشَرَ: fathas over the ʿayn, the shīn and the rā'; عشر (L04, L07) and عشرة (L06): no signs. كلّ (L03, L07): a shadda over the lām.

L04: اثنَيْ: a fatha over the nūn, between the three dots of the thā' and the dot of the nūn, and a round sukun over the yā'. جزءًا (L04, L05, L07 twice, L08): after the zāy the hamza with the fathatan above it in one cluster (3.6-4.0 x 5.8-6.1 pt), before the alif. بُعْده: a damma over the bā' and a round sukun over the ʿayn; البعد (L08): no signs.
L06: كلَّها: over the lām a shadda with a fatha above it (two marks).
L08: اجزاء and الضوء: the bare hamza on the line (2.9 x 2.9 pt in الضوء, after the wāw); no full stop stands after الضوء (4 x and both copies).

L09: النِّسَب: a shadda over the nūn, above its dot, a kasra under it and a fatha over the sīn. رَسَمْنا: a fatha over the rā', a fatha over the sīn and a round sukun over the mīm. الدائرتَيْن: a fatha over the tā', above its two dots, and a round sukun over the yā'. وبَيَّنَّاهما: a fatha over the bā' and, over the yā' and over the nūn, a shadda with a fatha above it (two marks each).
L10: إِن: the hamza and its kasra in one sort under the alif. شاء: the bare hamza on the line. اللّٰه: a shadda and the small upright alif over the second lām. The full stop after تعالى.

figures.note: the figure for the moon's light: the circle of the sun about ب with its level diameter ا ج; the upright axis from the top of the sun's circle through the centre of the earth, a filled disc with the letter ي and the word «الارض», down to the middle of the last circle of the moon; ten circles of the moon, their centres on a circle of 145.0 pt about the earth, 20 degrees apart on its left half, from the conjunction at the top (centre ن) to the opposition at the foot (centre ز), the eight between them with the centre د; in each circle the line ك ط, at right angles to the direction of the sun, bounds the dark half, which is hatched, and in the eight circles between the first and the last the line م ل, at right angles to the direction of the earth, crosses the whole circle; the words «مظلم» in the dark half of the first circle and «منير» in the lit half of the last; at the right of the axis a dashed arc from the first circle to the last and, upright along it, the words «وحكم هذا النصف مثل النصف الآخر». Measured on the master scan at 1200 dpi (scratch fig/f1058.py and fig/m1058_a ... g.py): the eleven circles are least-squares fits to the middle of their strokes where no other ink runs into them (rms 0.09 to 0.14 pt); the axis is one straight line through its clean stretches (they keep within 0.27 pt of it) and ends on the line ك ط of the last circle; the lines ك ط are fitted to their edge on the lit side and the lines م ل to their clear part, whose run through the hatching was found again from the unbroken ink along it (within 0.75 degrees and 0.4 pt of the same line; in the ninth circle within 1 pt); each line is drawn between its meetings with the fitted circle, with its measured thickness. The hatching of each dark half is drawn as a regular set of parallel lines with the direction, the mean distance (1.33 to 1.44 pt), the place and the thickness (0.42 to 0.56 pt) measured in that half away from its letters; the engraved lines are not quite even, and 63 to 81 per cent of the ink of the drawn lines falls on printed ones. The dashed arc is a circle fitted to the centres of its 90 dashes (rms 0.12 pt), drawn with their median length and gap between its meetings with the first and the last circle. The disc of the earth has the radius of its printed ink (the mean of its width, its height beside the axis and its area). The 59 letters and words are set at the centres of their printed ink; a letter that touches a line of the figure is measured up to that line, and the letters in the dark halves are measured after the hatching was taken out of the image (an opening of 0.36 pt)
